description.short_caption: Acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelson) stain showing branching filamentous structures.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelson) stain from a culture. The field contains branching, filamentous structures that stain bright red against a pale green background. These features are characteristic of acid-fast organisms, such as Nocardia species or Mycobacterium species. The branching morphology is particularly suggestive of Nocardia.
visible_findings: Bright red staining on Ziehl-Neelson stain

description.short_caption: Lateral chest radiograph showing thoracic structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a lateral chest radiograph displaying the thoracic cavity. The image shows the lung fields, spine, and diaphragm. There is evidence of increased radiodensity in the lower lung fields, which may suggest consolidation or fluid accumulation. The heart and mediastinal structures are partially visible. The image quality is adequate for interpretation, with clear visualization of bony and soft tissue structures.
visible_findings: increased radiodensity in lower lung fields
heart and mediastinal structures partially visible

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing cavitary lesion in the right lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates a cavitary lesion in the right lung, with surrounding consolidation and ground-glass opacities. The lesion appears irregular with thickened walls, suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process. The left lung shows no comparable abnormalities. The mediastinum and bony structures appear unremarkable in this slice.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right lung
normal left lung in this slice

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates significant abnormalities in both lungs. The left lung shows areas of consolidation with air bronchograms, suggesting alveolar filling processes. The right lung exhibits patchy ground-glass opacities and consolidation. There is no clear evidence of pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The mediastinum appears central, and no gross abnormalities of the heart or great vessels are visible.
visible_findings: air bronchograms in the left lung
patchy ground-glass opacities in the right lung

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing right-sided pleural effusion.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing evidence of a right-sided pleural effusion, indicated by blunting of the right costophrenic angle and increased opacification in the right lower lung field. The left lung appears clear, and the cardiac silhouette is within normal limits. The trachea is midline, and there is no visible pneumothorax. The skeletal structures, including the clavicles and ribs, appear intact.
visible_findings: blunting of the right costophrenic angle
increased opacification in the right lower lung field
